note: How the city sounds (SND-001 to SND-012; F-SND-WORLD, F-SND-ACTION and F-SND-MUSIC level 1). Every sound is made in code from these recipes, so there are no audio files to license. Gains are 0..1 before the mix, distances in metres, frequencies in Hz, times in seconds, hours as HH:MM. All values are [ASSUMPTION] until the owner has listened. Checked by Tools/worldgen/test_world.py.

podcasts.note: Talk on the car radio (SND-014). Hosts are voiced as wordless syllables in their own pitch, the way residents speak (Q-14: text first), and each line is shown as a caption. Where a show is now comes from the world clock, as a broadcast would: the same line at the same moment for everyone.

episodes.title: Market day
lines: mira
Good morning, Old Town. This is Tram Street Talk, and I'm Mira.
teo
And I'm Teo. Mira, I walked through Market Square at dawn and the stalls were already up.
mira
They always are. The flower stall sets up first. You can smell it from the fountain.
teo
I bought three apples and somehow left with a plant.
mira
That is how market day works. Nobody leaves with only what they came for.
teo
Is it true the busker knows only four songs?
mira
Four songs, played with feeling. That counts as a big repertoire round here.
teo
Fair. If you're heading over, the tram stops right by the square.
mira
Bring a bag. Bring two. We'll be back after the bell.

episodes.title: Catching the tram
lines: teo
You're listening to Tram Street Talk. Today, the tram.
mira
Our favourite slow, cream coloured friend.
teo
People ask why it rings twice. Once when it stops, once when it leaves.
mira
So you know to hurry. Or, if you're like me, to wave sadly as it goes.
teo
The commuters ride it out of town in the morning and back again at night.
mira
And the window seats on the left get the sun at the end of the day.
teo
A local secret, now shared with the whole town.
mira
Sorry, everyone. See you on the left side.

episodes.title: Rainy day plans
lines: mira
If the sky turns grey, where do you go in Old Town?
teo
Fountain Library. It's warm, it's quiet, and nobody minds if you nap.
mira
I'd say the Old Town Museum. You can learn something and stay dry.
teo
Or the Palace Cinema, with a paper bag of something sweet.
mira
Then a café after. Café Mina does a very good hot chocolate.
teo
That's three plans and a dessert. Nobody needs to be bored.
mira
That's our show. Be kind to each other out there.

episodes.title: Night walk
lines: oskar
This is The Quiet Hour. Take a breath. There's nowhere you need to be.
oskar
Tonight, a walk. Start at the fountain and listen to the water.
oskar
Turn up Mill Street. The lanterns are lit and the windows glow amber.
oskar
Somewhere a cat is deciding whether to cross the road. It decides not to.
oskar
At Linden Park the crickets have taken over the evening.
oskar
Sit on a bench. Count the windows still awake. One. Two. Three.
oskar
That's enough for tonight. Sleep well, Old Town.

episodes.title: Letters from listeners
lines: june
Welcome to The Quiet Hour. I'm June, reading your letters tonight.
june
Someone writes: I moved here last spring and I still get lost. Is that normal?
oskar
Completely normal. The streets are a grid, but the gardens hide the corners.
june
Another listener says the baker gave her an extra roll for no reason.
oskar
There's always a reason. The reason is that it was a good day.
june
And one more: what's the best time to see the town?
oskar
Just after sunset, when the lamps come on one by one.
june
Thank you for writing. Keep the letters coming.
